description: Procedural (scripting) expression evaluation goes through the SAME AST operator semantics as row expressions. The headline is boolean OR, which the old hand-rolled procedural evaluator mis-evaluated as string CONCATENATION - so 'false OR false' produced a non-empty and therefore TRUTHY string and every such IF was taken. Both directions of OR are pinned, along with AND, NOT, comparison over arithmetic, and the unary operators: unary minus maps to the shared NEGATE operator while unary plus is folded to the identity at build time and no longer creates a UnaryExpression, so both must still evaluate correctly including nested as the operand of a binary operator. Converted 1:1 from scripting/ProceduralExpressionEvalTest (now retired); each condition is run through the same IF ... THEN RETURN 1 ... RETURN 0 shape the Java used.

steps.sql: BEGIN IF (1 = 2 OR 1 = 1) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (1 = 2 OR 1 = 3) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (1 = 1 AND 2 = 2) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (1 = 1 AND 2 = 3) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (NOT (1 = 2)) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (NOT (1 = 1)) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (2 + 3 = 5) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (10 - 4 > 5) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (-3 < 0) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (+3 = 3) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
BEGIN IF (10 + -4 = 6) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN 0; END
